note: Single source of truth for the setup wizard: read by the Layer-0 worksheet (site.Data / import), scripts/setup.py, and the AGENTS.md interview. Prompt/help strings are the future i18n surface. Keep ids unique; every 'config' question needs both targets; every content_target must have a template.

questions.help: Used as the site title and woven into the code-of-conduct and start-here pages.

questions.prompt: A one-line tagline for your community?
questions.help: One warm sentence: who it is for and that newcomers are welcome.

questions.prompt: Where will the site's repository live?
questions.help: Prefer a shared community org over a personal account, so the site outlives any one organizer's access. Recorded only, this writes no config.

questions.prompt: What URL will the site be deployed at?
questions.help: Deploying to GitHub Pages under a subpath (e.g. /my-club/)? Include it, the theme handles subpaths.
A root-absolute path like /images/logo.png. 'Text-only for now' is a fine answer, skip it and the wordmark shows.

questions.prompt: Which code of conduct will you adopt?
questions.help: Adopt an established one rather than writing your own. The Contributor Covenant is common; Python-adjacent groups often use the PSF Code of Conduct. Recorded only.
A code of conduct needs a named reporting contact, not just a page. A shared inbox is better than one person.

questions.prompt: Where do people RSVP / register for events?
questions.help: A Meetup, Luma, or Eventbrite URL, or skip if you take RSVPs another way.

questions.prompt: A link to your community chat? (Discord, Slack, Matrix, Zulip)
questions.help: The community lives in chat between events. Set this and a 'Join the chat' button appears in the hero and footer.

questions.prompt: Add a social link (label + URL)? Repeat for each.
questions.help: Instagram, Mastodon, an email, whatever your community actually uses. Skippable, and repeatable.

questions.prompt: Invite people to speak? (adds a 'Your name here?' card to the speakers list)
questions.help: Turn on if you run talks and want to recruit speakers. Off by default.
